title: Excessive progression in weekly running distance and risk of running-related injuries: an association which varies according to type of injury
publisher: Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy
claims: A total of 874 healthy novice runners were recruited; 873 were included in the analysis and 202 sustained a running-related injury.
Runners were grouped by weekly distance progression: less than 10% or regression, 10% to 30%, and more than 30%.
No statistically significant difference in injury rates was found across the three progression groups.
Distance-related injuries were more frequent in the group progressing more than 30% than in the group progressing less than 10%, with a hazard ratio of 1.59 (95% CI 0.96 to 2.66; P = .07).
The authors conclude that novice runners may be well advised to progress their weekly distance by less than 30% per week over a two-week period.

原文：“an increased rate of sustaining an injury was observed in those runners who progressed their weekly running distance by greater than 30% compared with those who progressed less than 10% (HR = 1.59; 95% CI: 0.96, 2.66; P = .07)”。数值与 claim 完全一致，且 claim 保留了 P = .07，未谎称显著。
